content:
I fully admit that my DIY iPhone photography accessory looks ridiculous — but it genuinely makes using my phone for photos more practical and enjoyable.

It started as a solution to a specific video shoot problem, but I ended up using it far more than I expected…

One of the biggest divides in the compact camera world is whether or not a camera has a viewfinder. Photographers used to get very worked up about electronic viewfinders (EVF) versus optical ones, but EVFs are now so good that almost nobody cares any more.

Whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder offers real advantages over composing with the rear screen, especially in harsh sunlight. Even at maximum brightness, it's very hard to see what you're shooting when the sun is strong, and screen reflections get in the way.

In London this has rarely been a serious problem, but this summer we've had record-breaking heatwaves and, frankly, it feels like we haven't seen a cloud or any rain for about thirty years.

But it's more than that for me. I also think there's a psychological difference between only seeing what's in the frame of a photo and being able to see everything around you while you shoot. Sometimes it's precisely this sense of immersion that makes me reach for a dedicated camera rather than my phone.

When I chose a video camera a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was clearly the hot pick, but the lack of a viewfinder gave me pause. In the end I decided it wasn't a big issue for me because I'd mainly be using it indoors, and when I needed to shoot outside, a large screen with a sun hood solved most of the problems.

But sometimes I want a more compact shooting setup, not the full rig with a monitor, so I found a simple accessory suited to outdoor use. It's a combination of a sun hood and a magnifying lens that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, effectively giving you an optical viewfinder.

I was about to shoot a project that required recording with both the BMPCC 4K and my iPhone 16 Pro Max. I did a quick test on location and found the viewfinder accessory incredibly useful. The BMPCC 4K and iPhone screens are roughly the same size, so I wondered whether this accessory might also work on the iPhone.

Of course the iPhone has no magnetic attachment, but it's light enough that holding it up to the magnifying lens is no problem at all. Surprisingly it works brilliantly, especially when I use the Camera Control button as a shutter.

Since then I've used it to shoot in a variety of situations, and whether it's being able to see the screen more easily in harsh sunlight or that sense of immersion, I've thoroughly enjoyed using it. My iPhone became my main camera several years ago, and with this homemade modification I feel it's enough even more often.

Is it absurd, or genius? Let me know your thoughts in the comments. If you think it's genius, sorry — the product I bought seems to have been discontinued, and I haven't seen anything similar designed for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, please post a link in the comments.
